intro.label: What You'll Spend
intro.heading: Bedlington Terrier First-Year Cost Breakdown
intro.html:
Bedlingtons are moderately expensive to own — the professional grooming is an unavoidable recurring cost, but food costs are modest for a small breed. The primary financial risk factor is Copper Toxicosis: if a dog is not from DNA-cleared parents and develops this liver disease, treatment is expensive and outcomes are uncertain. Buying from health-tested breeders and enrolling in pet insurance before the first vet visit are the most important financial protections.

care.label: Biggest Costs
care.heading: Where Bedlington Ownership Gets Expensive
care.html:
Professional Grooming: The Fixed Recurring Cost

Unlike dogs with wash-and-wear coats, the Bedlington requires professional grooming every 6–8 weeks to maintain the breed's distinctive shape. At $60–$100 per appointment (depending on location and groomer), this adds $450–$850 per year as a fixed ongoing cost. Factor this in before buying — it's not optional if you want the coat to look correct and stay healthy.

Copper Toxicosis: The Major Health Financial Risk

Copper Toxicosis is a liver disease unique to the breed. Dogs from untested parents who develop the condition require liver biopsies ($500–$1,000), ongoing copper-restricted diets (specialized, more expensive food), and medication (D-penicillamine, $50–$150/month). In advanced cases, liver failure requires intensive care. This is why DNA testing of both parents is non-negotiable and why buying from untested breeders creates real financial risk. Pet insurance enrolled before the first vet visit covers most of these treatment costs.

PRA and Eye Care

Progressive Retinal Atrophy has no treatment, but managing a blind dog's environment (baby gates, consistent layout, no furniture rearrangements) has minimal financial cost. Regular CAER eye exams ($50–$80) are worth including in the annual vet budget even after the puppy year.

special.label: Lifetime Budget
special.heading: Estimating Lifetime Bedlington Costs
special.html:
With an 11–16 year lifespan — one of the longer ranges for any breed — the Bedlington represents a long financial commitment. The good news is that dogs from health-tested parents tend to live out their full lifespan without major interventions.

ScenarioEstimated Lifetime Cost
Healthy dog from DNA-cleared parents$22,000–$38,000
Dog requiring treatment for hip dysplasia or PRA$28,000–$45,000
Dog with Copper Toxicosis (untested parents)$35,000–$60,000+

The difference between the first and third rows is largely preventable by buying from DNA-tested breeders and carrying pet insurance. The grooming cost is unavoidable regardless of health status.

faq.q: What does a Bedlington Terrier puppy cost from a reputable breeder?
faq.a: $1,500–$2,500 from health-testing breeders. The premium reflects the cost of DNA testing for Copper Toxicosis, PRA, and hip clearances for both parents. Cheaper puppies from untested breeders carry a real risk of Copper Toxicosis — a liver disease with high treatment costs and uncertain outcomes. The extra cost upfront is significantly cheaper than treating a dog from untested parents.

faq.q: Is pet insurance worth it for a Bedlington Terrier?
faq.a: Yes — particularly for coverage against Copper Toxicosis if buying without full parental clearances, and for hip dysplasia and eye conditions. Enroll before the first vet visit to avoid pre-existing condition exclusions. Monthly premiums of $35–$70 for a small breed are manageable given the potential treatment costs.

faq.q: How much does Bedlington grooming cost annually?
faq.a: Plan for $500–$800 per year for professional grooming at 6–8 week intervals. This is a fixed recurring cost that doesn't go away — it's the maintenance price of the breed's distinctive coat. Add home brushing supplies (slicker brush, metal comb) as a one-time setup cost of $40–$80.
